sections.title: Student Development in College Environments
sections.description: Student development refers to the ways a student grows, progresses, or enhances their developmental capabilities through enrollment in higher education. In this course, we will examine student development in college settings using the theoretical frameworks of adult development, positive psychology, and social cognitive theory. We will focus on the first three steps of adult development: identity development, relationship skills development, and career development. In this course, we will use an evidence-based approach by learning to interpret correlational studies (quantitative) and by conducting in-depth interviews (qualitative). Additionally, the course will focus on student development through the lens of diversity, equity, belonging, and inclusion, exploring how college environments can foster the psychological conditions essential for student development.

sections.title: Student Development in College Environments
sections.description: An overview of college student development theory is offered in this course. Specifically, three families of theory are explored: 1) Psychosocial and identity, 2) cognitive-structural, and 3) environmental. The theories are discussed in terms of their foundations, constructs, and applicability to work in various functional areas of higher education.
